person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: null-result
span.quote: Hence the Entscheidungsproblem cannot be solved.

span.label: computability of real numbers
span.quote: The "computable" numbers may be described briefly as the real numbers whose expressions as a decimal are calculable by finite means.

span.label: mathematical-proof
span.quote: I shall enunciate a number of theorems about computability, but I shall prove only (ii) and a theorem similar to (iii).

span.label: The case that the machine definition captures everything intuitively computable can only be argued by appeal to intuition, which the author calls mathematically unsatisfactory.
span.quote: Al I arguments which can be given are bound to be, fundamentally, appeals to intuition, and for this reason rather unsatisfactory mathematically.

span.label: A consistency proof required for the recursion result is not supplied.
span.quote: I shall not give the proof of consistency of %n.

span.label: Classical analysis does not carry over unchanged: a computable bounded increasing sequence of computable numbers need not have a computable limit.
span.quote: Owing to this restriction of Dedekind's theorem, we cannot say that a computable bounded increasing sequence of computable numbers has a computable limit.

span.label: The computable numbers are strictly narrower than the definable numbers.
span.quote: The computable numbers do not, however, include all definable numbers, and an example is given of a definable number which is not computable.

span.label: The definition of the central term is justified by an empirical claim about human beings, and the justification is postponed.
span.quote: No real attempt will be made to justify the definitions given until we reach § 9. For the present I shall only say that the justification lies in the fact that the human memory is necessarily limited

span.label: The class defined does not exhaust the numbers that can be named, and the paper supplies a counterexample.
span.quote: The computable numbers do not, however, include all definable numbers, and an example is given of a definable number which is not computable

span.label: There is no procedure that decides the property the whole construction turns on.
span.quote: we have no general process for doing this in a finite number of steps. In fact, by applying the diagonal process argument correctly, we can show that there cannot be any such general process

span.label: The translation between the paper's informal vocabulary and its machine vocabulary is valid only if the central definition is, and the paper says so in the same breath.
span.quote: The expression "there is a general process for determining..." has been used throughout this section as equivalent to "there is a machine which will determine ... ". This usage can be justified if and only if we can justify our definition of "computable"

span.label: circular and circle-free - THE DISTINCTION THE FIELD LATER RENAMED 'HALTING', WITH THE POLES SWAPPED IN VALUE: a machine is circular if it never writes more than finitely many symbols of the first kind, and circle-free otherwise, so the machine that runs forever is the SUCCESSFUL one here and the word 'halting' names the failure case as though it were the subject
span.quote: If a computing machine never writes down more than a finite number of symbols of the first kind, it will be called circular. Otherwise it is said to be circle-free

span.label: 'a general process for determining' - DECLARED EQUIVALENT TO 'a machine which will determine': the paper states its own translation rule between informal and machine vocabulary, says it holds throughout the section, and makes it conditional on the definition of computable being justified
span.quote: The expression "there is a general process for determining..." has been used throughout this section as equivalent to "there is a machine which will determine ... ". This usage can be justified if and only if we can justify our definition of "computable"

span.label: the computer - A HUMAN BEING: throughout the argument of section 9 'the computer' is a person observing symbols and holding a state of mind, with a bound on how many squares he can observe at once; the word now denotes the machine that was built to replace him
span.quote: The behaviour of the computer at any moment is determined by the symbols which he is observing, and his " state of mind " at that moment. We may suppose that there is a bound B to the number of symbols or squares which the computer can observe at one moment

span.label: computable - AS WRITABLE-DOWN-BY-A-MACHINE: the definition is stated in terms of a machine producing the decimal, not in terms of a formula or a rule
span.quote: According to my definition, a number is computable if its decimal can be written down by a machine

span.label: contradicts → Hilbert's Entscheidungsproblem (the hope for a general decision procedure)
span.quote: Hilbertian Entscheidungsproblem can have no solution

span.label: replicates → Alonzo Church, "An unsolvable problem of elementary number theory" and "A note on the Entscheidungsproblem"
span.quote: Church also reaches similar conclusions about the EntscheidungsproblemJ.

span.label: builds-on → Church's notion of effective calculability (lambda-definability)
span.quote: In a recent paper Alonzo Church f has introduced an idea of "effective calculability", which is equivalent to my "computability", but is very differently defined.

span.label: circle-free —distinct-from→ circular
span.quote: If a computing machine never writes down more than a finite number of symbols of the first kind, it will be called circular. Otherwise it is said to be circle-free

span.label: effective calculability —same-as→ computability
span.quote: The proof of equivalence between "computability" and "effective calculability" is outlined in an appendix to the present paper

span.label: A number is computable if its decimal can be written down by a machine operating by finite means; Turing defines such machines (tape, m-configurations, scanned symbols) capturing everything naturally regarded as computable.
span.quote: According to my definition, a number is computable if its decimal can be written down by a machine.

span.label: A single UNIVERSAL computing machine can compute any computable sequence — the basis for resolving the Entscheidungsproblem, since some definable numbers are provably not computable.
span.quote: It is possible to invent a single machine which can be used to compute any computable sequence.

span.label: Computable numbers do not include all definable numbers, yet the class of computable numbers is enumerable.
span.quote: The computable numbers do not, however, include all definable numbers, and an example is given of a definable number which is not computable.

span.label: computable number
span.quote: The "computable" numbers may be described briefly as the real numbers whose expressions as a decimal are calculable by finite means.

span.label: universal computing machine
span.quote: It is possible to invent a single machine which can be used to compute any computable sequence.

span.label: m-configuration
span.quote: which will be called " m-configurations ". The machine is supplied with a " t a p e" (the analogue of paper) running through it
